title: Union Budget 2026-27: capital expenditure vs effective capital expenditure

verification_claim.text: In Budget Estimates 2026-27, Union Government capital expenditure is ₹12.22 lakh crore, while effective capital expenditure is ₹17.15 lakh crore because grants for creation of capital assets are added to direct capital expenditure.

definitions: Budget Estimate (BE) is a budgeted projection, not actual realised expenditure.
Effective capital expenditure equals Union capital expenditure plus grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
evidence.title: Statements of Fiscal Policy under the FRBM Act, Union Budget 2026-27
evidence.evidence_summary: The document projects ₹12.22 lakh crore of capital expenditure in BE 2026-27, including ₹2.0 lakh crore of capital support to states through SASCI.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
evidence.title: Statements of Fiscal Policy under the FRBM Act, Union Budget 2026-27
evidence.evidence_summary: The same document projects ₹4.93 lakh crore of grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets and ₹17.15 lakh crore of effective capital expenditure.

research_summary: The Budget distinguishes direct Union capital expenditure from effective capital expenditure. BE 2026-27 direct capital expenditure is ₹12.22 lakh crore. Adding ₹4.93 lakh crore of grants for creation of capital assets produces effective capital expenditure of ₹17.15 lakh crore. These are budget estimates, not actual expenditure.

locked_claims.text: Capital expenditure in BE 2026-27 is ₹12.22 lakh crore.
Grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets in BE 2026-27 are ₹4.93 lakh crore.
Effective capital expenditure in BE 2026-27 is ₹17.15 lakh crore.

material_caveats: ₹17.15 lakh crore is effective capital expenditure, not direct Union capital expenditure alone.
All three values are Budget Estimates for 2026-27, not actual realised expenditure.
prohibited_claims: The Union Government will definitely spend ₹17.15 lakh crore directly as capital expenditure.
₹17.15 lakh crore is actual expenditure already incurred.
The ₹4.93 lakh crore grants are separate from effective capital expenditure rather than included within it.
